A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Contra4. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–K are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, OneLLM fine-tuning experiments, human inspection of filtering quality, and captioning results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds human performance measured on 50 test examples.

M1.justification: The four-stage data-generation pipeline, MF/UF/PMF/PUF filters, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Section 3 explicitly inserts Enc before projection, clarifying existing encoder processing without establishing a changed architecture or procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same caption sources in Table 4 and the same image, audio, video, and 3D selection task. The added human evaluation samples the existing test set without introducing new task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Section 6 adds human performance as a reference comparator. Table 2 retains the same model comparators: CREMA, X-InstructBLIP, OneLLM, Gemini-2.0, and the Caption Baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds an evaluation involving 50 test examples and two independent annotators. The existing 120-sample filtering inspection, model evaluation settings, and OneLLM fine-tuning protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The filtering-quality analyses, modality breakdowns, and fine-tuning ablations are retained in Tables 1, 5, and 7 and Figures 4, 5, and 8. The added human reference score and revised illustrative examples introduce no separate ablation, robustness test, or error analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions explicitly report single-run model accuracy. v2 adds no confidence intervals, significance tests, seeds, or repeated-model-run information; its new human average has no accompanying uncertainty or inter-annotator agreement estimate.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports 92% average human accuracy on 50 test examples. Existing numerical results remain unchanged, including CREMA's 56% overall accuracy and OneLLM's improvement from 32% to 50%. The human score is additional subset evidence, not a same-setting model performance improvement.

T1.justification: Section 3 expands P_M(x) to P_M(Enc(x)), making the already described encoder/projection processing explicit. This is a clarification of the representation, with no substantive change to the formal task, assumptions, mathematical reasoning, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the four-modality benchmark, caption-based MoM-RTC generation, and evidence of model difficulty despite fine-tuning. The abstract clarifies relative improvement versus absolute accuracy without changing its claims or reported values.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly explains choosing OneLLM for native point-cloud processing to avoid input-conversion confounds. Section 6 interprets the human result as evidence of a human–model performance gap. The applicability boundaries and limitations in Section 7 are unchanged.

D1.justification: The generation prompts, hardware, decoding parameters, LoRA settings, captioning models, annotation-interface documentation, and project access information are retained. The new human sample size and annotator count concern the added evaluation protocol.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and benchmark positioning in Table 3 are unchanged. No prior work is added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited explanatory additions in Sections 3, 5, and 6, clarifies the abstract's accuracy wording, and adds acknowledgments. The section sequence and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 9 revises example panels, including audio descriptions, the tire-skidding question, and circled answer choices. Table 2, Table 7, and several figures move within the layout; their existing results are retained. There is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added human evaluation provides useful evidence of task solvability, while the input-pipeline clarification, OneLLM selection rationale, and revised Figure 9 improve clarity. These are limited gains: the main experiments are unchanged, and the human comparison reports neither uncertainty nor model scores on the identical 50-example subset, limiting conclusions about the precise performance gap.
